page: Amazon Web Services p4d.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It integrates 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at 3.0 GHz, alongside 1152 GB of DDR4 system memory. Hardware acceleration is provided by eight NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs delivering an aggregate 320 GB of VRAM. High-speed local data handling is supported by 8000 GB of bundled NVMe SSD instance storage and a 400 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface.

Benchmark evaluations indicate high multi-threaded compute and data transfer capabilities. The instance scores in the top tier for stress-ng multi-core CPU testing, PassMark CPU benchmarks, Clang compilation, and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate high cached throughput alongside 78.21 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. However, single-threaded processing benchmarks, such as single-core Geekbench and compression tasks, align with mid-range baselines, and host CPU-driven LLM text generation yields relatively modest throughput across tested models.

Given the density of eight interconnected A100 GPUs, massive host memory, and direct NVMe storage, this server minimizes network bottlenecks during inter-node synchronization and large data ingest. It is best configured for distributed deep learning model training, GPU-accelerated scientific simulations, high-performance rendering, and intensive data pre-processing pipelines that fully saturate dedicated accelerator and network resources.
